parsed.why: Strong state public-accommodations law, protected facilities access, hate-crime enforcement and working care protections raise it well above parent, but national border/document screening and pending ballot pressure cap it.
State executive order defines sex biologically, backs single-sex spaces, lacks public-accommodations and GI hate-crime coverage, and documented custody harm; local hostility clearly below parent.

Public-accommodations protection, GI hate-crime law, shield statutes and gender-neutral single-user facilities make it strongly protective locally, though national border and document exposure remains.

Government-building bathroom/locker ban with complaint mechanism and inaccessible documentary defence is a traveler-facing facility restriction; limited nondiscrimination law and care ban add exposure.
Broad public-facilities ban with civil cause of action, no state GI nondiscrimination or hate-crime law, and restrictive marker rules create the heaviest local exposure among the five.
